title: Guardrail
description: An assertion about agent behavior. Enforced at runtime (halt / retry / escalate / log-only / compensate per guardrail) AND in CI (blocks builds). Same definition, two enforcement paths — no drift between what tests check and what prod enforces. Zero-LLM checks are default (fast, deterministic); LLM-judge scorers are an opt-in class with explicit cost declaration. Schema-version 1.1.0 matches the `Guardrail` type: `check` is required, a `retry` action needs `maxAttempts`, `kind` and `on-violation` accept any non-empty string (the built-ins are listed as `examples`), and `sandbox` / `limits` / `network` / `needsSpec` are allowed.

description.description: What this guardrail guarantees, and what happens if violated.

kind.description: How the guardrail is checked. Open string: the engine dispatches it to the execution strategy registered for that kind, and `defineGuardrail` requires a registered check of the same kind. Built-in kinds: 'zero-llm' = pure function over run trace (default, fast, deterministic). 'llm-judge' = uses a model to score (opt-in, costs money). 'external' = evaluated outside the engine by a caller-registered strategy (the built-in 'external' strategy returns an error). Adapters can register strategies for their own kinds.

check.description: Id of the check in the CheckRegistry. For zero-llm: a built-in check ('must-cite', 'never-call-tool', 'max-tool-calls', 'output-matches', 'tool-order', 'required-substring', 'forbidden-substring') or a custom check id. For llm-judge: the id of a registered check of kind 'llm-judge' (the judge is configured by config and judgeCapabilities). For external and adapter kinds: an id the kind's strategy understands. Required since schema-version 1.1.0 (`defineGuardrail` already failed without a registered check).

config.description: Check-specific configuration. Interpreted by the check implementation.

configSchema.description: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) of the check's config, for a check that is pack code: the pack index's `configSchema`, which a deployment keeps on the guardrails it registers. The runtime checks a guardrail's `config` against it at registration, for any guardrail naming that check, and the pack service checks it on every call. Optional; a runtime-declaration field like `codeArtifactRef`.

scope.description: When this guardrail applies: 'always' (every run), 'ci-only' (blocks CI, not runtime), 'runtime-only' (runtime enforcement, not CI), or a per-agent/per-flow selector.

budget.description: For llm-judge guardrails: cost budget per invocation. Declarative — not enforced by the runtime.

sandbox.description: Isolation posture the runtime enforces around the check's handler. Same values as a tool's `sandbox`. Added in schema-version 1.1.0.

limits.description: Sandbox-enforced resource caps while the check runs. Same shape as a tool's `limits`. Added in schema-version 1.1.0.

network.description: Network egress policy the sandbox honors while the check runs. Discriminated on `kind`; same shape as a tool's `network`. Added in schema-version 1.1.0.

needsSpec.description: Typed discriminated needs of the check (env / secrets / config / capabilities / bindings). Same shape as a tool's `needsSpec`. Added in schema-version 1.1.0.

codeArtifactRef.description: Handler-artifact pointer for the guardrail's check implementation. Discriminated on `kind`: `oci` is the deploy-pipeline shape (image + module path + artifactVersion); `filesystem` is the local-development shape — absolute host path at the check module. Production servers SHOULD reject `filesystem`.

judgeCapabilities.description: For llm-judge guardrails: capability declaration for the judge model. Routed through `@kindgi/capabilities` over the providers bound for evaluation; when the caller passes a tenant policy (an agent turn passes its own), the judge is routed under it. BYO judges supported.

on-violation.description: What happens when the guardrail fires. Open string: any non-empty name is accepted here, and an action handler registered under that name applies it; when the caller evaluates with an action-handler registry, a name with no handler fails with `unknown-action`. Built-in actions: 'halt' = fail the run. 'retry' = re-execute the step (needs `retry.maxAttempts`). 'escalate' = route to HITL review. 'log-only' = record but don't block. 'compensate' = invoke a compensation action.

escalateTo.description: For on-violation = 'escalate': reviewer role or queue id.

compensateWith.description: For on-violation = 'compensate': tool id to invoke as compensation.

agents.description: Agent ids this guardrail applies to. Empty = all agents.

flows.description: Flow ids this guardrail applies to. Empty = all flows.

tenants.description: Tenant ids this guardrail applies to. Empty = all tenants.
